races.title: State Assembly, District 17
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Matt Haney
cands.bio: Democrat and attorney who has represented Assembly District 17 (eastern San Francisco) since May 2022. Previously a San Francisco Supervisor (2019–2022) and school board member, first elected in 2012. Earlier worked as a legislative aide to a state senator and as national policy director of The Dream Corps.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action.
President Barack Obama endorsed him in his 2016 school board re-election.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from him on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, guns, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. We found no stated pledge on refusing foreign-linked or big-donor money. His campaign site speaks of community policing but gives no position on police pay, pensions or penalties for disorder. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties in the pages reviewed. We could not establish when, if ever, he moved to California, since he was born here.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Santa Cruz County, raised in the San Francisco Bay Area and attended public schools in Albany, California, and the record shows him living in San Francisco as an adult.

land.label: 2 documented positions for data centers or more development

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2022, San Francisco Supervisor 2019–2022, and San Francisco school board member from a 2012 election win to 2019. Earlier a legislative aide to a state senator, executive director of the UC Student Association, national policy director of The Dream Corps, tenant attorney and law lecturer.
qual.why: Several years of legislative service at the state and city level plus a law and policy career put him in the high range for a job of writing law and the budget.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: As a San Francisco Supervisor in October 2021, he supported a 495-unit apartment complex on a parking lot next to a BART station; the board voted it down 7-4. He also supported state action to make cities allow more housing and a local bill legalizing fourplexes on single-family lots.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says California must be a national leader in protecting a woman's right to choose.

cands.name: Manuel Noris-Barrera
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 17 in 2024 and 2026. He advanced from the 2024 primary and lost the general election to incumbent Matt Haney (D). He has held no public office, and no other career details were found.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California endorsed him in his 2024 Assembly District 17 race.
SF Family Voting Bloc (a Sway voting group run by Kartik Sathappan) listed him as a recommended candidate in 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Manuel Noris-Barrera was born or raised, when he came to California, or his work history. Because of that, his ties to California and his job fit for writing laws and the state budget could not be assessed. He has held no elected office that we found. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026, and we found no campaign website, questionnaire or interview stating his positions. We found no record of actions or statements on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. No controversies or foreign ties were found.
